The river that runs through London is the Thames.

The cohesion of the provided text is strong. The transitions and linking devices effectively connect the ideas. The first sentence introduces the problem of coral reefs. The second sentence, starting with "The increase in water temperature is also to blame," uses the additive phrase "also to blame" to link the new cause (temperature) to the previous one (acidification). The third sentence begins with "Fish populations that depend on these reefs," using the demonstrative "these" to refer back to the reefs mentioned earlier, thereby linking the impact on fish to the state of the reefs. Finally, the fourth sentence starts with "This situation," which acts as a summarizing reference to the preceding points about declining fish populations and reef health, and connects them to the broader impact on human communities. The logical flow from cause to effect to broader consequence is clear and well-supported by these linguistic links.
